title: Meet Abhijay, a 14-Year-Old Who Teaches Kids to Code
summary:
What were you doing when you were 14? Abhijay Potluri, from Boxborough, Massachusetts, started a nonprofit called Kids Who Teach. He teaches coding, public speaking, and problem-solving to kids in India, Indonesia, Uganda, and the U.S.

Abhijay got the idea during the COVID-19 pandemic, when he learned to code. "I realized kids could actually build things that help people," he says. He also helped organize a fundraiser for people affected by a fire near his home. "Kids in my school became homeless," he says. "What stuck with me was seeing every age show up: fourth graders donating next to adults."

Being a kid with big projects isn't always easy. "School, sports, and my projects all pile up on the same day," he says. Some people think kids can't make real change because they're young. "That gets to me," Abhijay says. But he plans out his day and gets things done.

His proudest moment? Teaching kids in so many different countries. His advice for other kids: "The hardest part is figuring out where to start. Once you make a plan, it gets a lot easier. You just need to take the first step."
why_it_matters: Abhijay's story shows that you don't have to wait until you are grown up to help others — one small plan can grow into something big.

background_read: A nonprofit (an organization that works to help people or solve a problem instead of making money) can be started by anyone — even a kid.
Coding means writing the instructions that tell a computer what to do, and free lessons online let kids in different countries learn it.
Other young people have made a difference too: Malala Yousafzai (a girl from Pakistan who spoke up for girls' education) won the Nobel Peace Prize while she was still a teenager.
